title: Olasılık
canDo: Geleceğe, şimdiye ve geçmişe dair olasılıkları ince derecelerle (bound to, may well, likely to, the chances are, I doubt whether) ifade edebilir, tahminlerimi gerekçelendirebilir ve geleceğe dair dengeli bir öngörü yazısı yazabilirim.
grammar: may well / might well / could well
be bound to / be sure to / be certain to
be (un)likely to / It is likely that / The chances are
geçmişe dair olasılık: is bound to have, may well have

liveClass.title: Kâhinler meclisi
liveClass.goal: Gruplar 2050 yılı için bir alan seçer (eğitim, ulaşım, sağlık, iş). Her grup 5 tahmin hazırlar ve her birinin olasılığını farklı yapılarla belirtir (bound to, may well, highly unlikely to). Sınıf her tahmin için kendi olasılık oyunu verir ve gruplar tahminlerini savunur.

lessons.title: Pekâlâ olabilir
lessons.goal: may well / might well / could well ve bound to / sure to yapılarıyla gelecek hakkında farklı derecelerde tahmin yapabilirim.

learn.explanation:
**Olasılık ölçeği (gelecek):**

| Kesinlik | Yapı | Örnek |
|---|---|---|
| ~%100 | **be bound to** + V1 | They're **bound to** be tired. |
| ~%100 | **be sure / certain to** + V1 | The stadium's **sure to** be full. |
| ~%90 | **will definitely / certainly** | It'll **definitely** rain. |
| ~%70 | **may well / might well / could well** + V1 | They **may well** win. |
| ~%70 | **will probably** / **probably won't** | He'll **probably** be late. |
| ~%50 | **may / might / could** + V1 | It **might** snow. |
| ~%30 | **might not / may not** | She **might not** come. |
| ~%5 | **definitely won't / certainly won't** | It **definitely won't** happen. |

**may well / might well / could well:** **well** eklemek olasılığı **artırır**.

- *It **might** rain.* (Belki.) → *It **might well** rain.* (Gayet muhtemel.)

**be bound to:** Konuşanın **mantıklı kanıta dayalı kesin tahmini**:

- *You've worked so hard. You're **bound to** pass.*
- *If you leave it there, someone **is bound to** steal it.*

**Zarfların yeri:**

- Olumlu cümlede **will'den sonra**: *It **will probably** rain.*
- Olumsuz cümlede **won't'tan önce**: *It **probably won't** rain.* (~~It won't probably~~)

examples.en: If you don't book now, the tickets are bound to sell out.
The new policy may well cause problems.
examples.tr: Yeni politika pekâlâ sorunlara yol açabilir.

examples.en: He probably won't get the job.

learn.turkishNote: Türkçede olasılık "kesin", "büyük ihtimalle", "belki", "pek sanmam" gibi kelimelerle ince ince ayarlanır; İngilizce de çok zengindir. "may well" Türkçedeki "pekâlâ" kelimesine çok yakındır ("Pekâlâ kazanabilirler"). Türkçe konuşanların en sık hatası zarfın yeridir: "It won't probably" yanlıştır; olumsuz cümlede "probably" won't'tan önce gelir.

lessons.title: Muhtemel ve pek olası değil
lessons.goal: be likely to, It is likely that, The chances are ve in all likelihood gibi yapılarla olasılığı resmî ve dengeli bir dille ifade edebilirim.

discover.title: Bir rapor: İşin geleceği
discover.body:
Over the next twenty years, artificial intelligence is likely to change the nature of work dramatically.

It is highly likely that many routine office tasks, such as data entry and scheduling, will be fully automated. Jobs in areas like customer service are also likely to be affected. However, it is unlikely that machines will replace jobs that require creativity, empathy or complex decision-making, at least in the foreseeable future.

The chances are that most workers will need to retrain at least once during their careers. In all likelihood, lifelong learning will become the norm rather than the exception.

There is also a strong possibility that working hours will become more flexible. Some experts even believe that a four-day week is likely to become common by 2040, although this is by no means certain.

questions.prompt: Which jobs are unlikely to be replaced?
questions.explanation: "jobs that require creativity, empathy or complex decision-making"

questions.prompt: What will most workers probably need to do?
questions.explanation: "most workers will need to retrain at least once"

learn.explanation:
**be likely / unlikely to + V1** (özne kişi ya da şey)

- *AI **is likely to** change work.*
- *He **is unlikely to** agree.*
- *Prices **are highly likely to** rise.* (çok muhtemel)

**It is likely / unlikely that + cümle**

- ***It is likely that** many tasks **will** be automated.*
- ***It is highly unlikely that** she **will** resign.*

**Dikkat:** **likely** bir **sıfattır**, zarf değil!

- ~~He will likely come.~~ (AmE'de kullanılır, ama İngiliz akademik yazısında genellikle tercih edilmez)
- ✓ *He **is likely to** come.* / ✓ *He will **probably** come.*

**Diğer yapılar:**

| Yapı | Örnek |
|---|---|
| **The chances are (that)** | **The chances are** most workers will retrain. |
| **There's a good / strong chance that** | **There's a good chance that** it'll rain. |
| **There's a strong possibility that** | **There's a strong possibility that** hours will change. |
| **In all likelihood,** (resmî) | **In all likelihood,** the plan will fail. |
| **The likelihood of** + isim / -ing | **The likelihood of** success is low. |
| **The chances of** + -ing **are slim** | **The chances of** finding him **are slim**. |

**Derecelendirme:** *highly / very / quite likely* — *highly / extremely unlikely*

examples.en: The new law is likely to be approved next month.
examples.tr: Yeni yasanın gelecek ay onaylanması muhtemel.

examples.en: It is highly unlikely that prices will fall.
examples.tr: Fiyatların düşmesi son derece düşük bir ihtimal.

examples.en: The chances of winning the lottery are extremely slim.
examples.tr: Piyangoyu kazanma ihtimali son derece düşük.

learn.turkishNote: Türkçede "-mesi muhtemel" yapısı ("onaylanması muhtemel") İngilizcede iki şekilde kurulabilir: "It is likely to be approved" ya da "It is likely that it will be approved". Türkçe konuşanların sık hatası, "likely"yi "probably" gibi zarf olarak kullanmaktır: "It will likely happen" Amerikan İngilizcesinde duyulur ama sınavlarda ve İngiliz akademik dilinde "It is likely to happen" daha güvenli bir tercihtir.

lessons.title: Olmuş olmalı, olmuş olabilir
lessons.goal: Şimdiki ve geçmiş zaman hakkında ileri düzey olasılık yapılarını (must be -ing, is bound to have, may well have, is likely to have) kullanabilirim.

lines.speaker: Aylin
lines.text: The package still hasn't arrived. It was supposed to come yesterday.

lines.speaker: Tarık

learn.explanation:
B2'de **must have / might have / can't have** yapılarını öğrendiniz. C1'de olasılık yapılarını **şimdiki** ve **geçmiş** zamanla birleştiriyoruz.

**Şimdi devam eden durum hakkında:**

| Yapı | Örnek |
|---|---|
| **must be + -ing** | He **must be having** a busy week. |
| **can't be + -ing** | She **can't be working**. It's Sunday. |
| **may / might be + -ing** | They **might be sleeping**. |
| **is bound to be + -ing** | He**'s bound to be waiting** for us. |

**Geçmiş hakkında:**

| Yapı | Kesinlik | Örnek |
|---|---|---|
| **is bound to have** + V3 | çok yüksek | It**'s bound to have been** left with a neighbour. |
| **must have** + V3 | çok yüksek | It **must have been** delivered. |
| **is likely to have** + V3 | yüksek | It**'s likely to have been** delivered to the wrong flat. |
| **may well / might well have** + V3 | gayet muhtemel | Someone **may well have** taken it. |
| **may / might / could have** + V3 | orta | It **might have** got lost. |
| **is unlikely to have** + V3 | düşük | He**'s unlikely to have** forgotten. |
| **can't / couldn't have** + V3 | imkânsız | It **can't have** been stolen. |

**Edilgen:** *It **is likely to have been** delivered.* / *It **may well have been** stolen.*

examples.en: She must be feeling nervous about the interview.
The email is bound to have gone to your spam folder.
He may well have missed the train.

learn.turkishNote: Türkçede "düşmüştür" (The email has probably gone) ve "düşmüş olmalı" (must have gone) gibi yapılar kesinliği ayarlar. İngilizcede "is bound to have" ve "is likely to have" bu derecelendirmeyi çok daha ince yapar. Türkçe konuşanlar geçmiş için "is likely that it was" demeye eğilimlidir; bu da doğrudur, ama "is likely to have been" daha kısa ve daha akademiktir.

options: It's bound to be left with a neighbour.
It's bound to have been left with a neighbour.
It may well have been stolen.

lessons.title: Emin misin?
lessons.goal: Kesinlik ve şüphe bildiren deyimsel ifadeleri (I doubt whether, I wouldn't be surprised if, it's a long shot, a foregone conclusion) doğal bir şekilde kullanabilirim.

discover.title: Seçim gecesi yorumları
discover.body:
Commentator 1: "With half the votes counted, it's looking like a foregone conclusion. There's no doubt that the governing party will win the most seats."

Commentator 2: "I wouldn't be so sure. I doubt whether they'll have a majority. The big cities haven't been counted yet."

Commentator 1: "True, but I'd be very surprised if the opposition won more than 40%."

Commentator 2: "I wouldn't be surprised if we saw a coalition. It's a long shot, but the smaller parties could well hold the balance of power."

Commentator 1: "The odds are against it. But anything can happen in politics. Against all odds, a new party won 15% of the vote four years ago."

options: That the governing party will win any seats
That the governing party will have a majority
That the votes will be counted
questions.explanation: "I doubt whether they'll have a majority."

questions.prompt: What surprising thing happened four years ago?
options: A new party won 15% of the vote.
questions.explanation: "a new party won 15% of the vote four years ago"

learn.explanation:
**Kesinlik:**

| İfade | Anlam |
|---|---|
| **There's no doubt that** ... | Hiç şüphe yok ki ... |
| **It's a foregone conclusion.** | Sonuç önceden belli. |
| **It's a dead cert.** (samimi) | Kesin. |
| **I'm (absolutely) convinced that** ... | ... olduğuna kesinlikle inanıyorum. |
| **Without a shadow of a doubt** | Hiç şüphesiz |

**Olasılık / şüphe:**

| İfade | Anlam |
|---|---|
| **I wouldn't be surprised if** + past | ... olsa şaşırmam (= muhtemel) |
| **I'd be (very) surprised if** + past | ... olsa çok şaşırırım (= pek olası değil) |
| **I doubt (whether / if / that)** ... | ... olacağından şüpheliyim |
| **I have my doubts about** ... | ... konusunda şüphelerim var |
| **It's a long shot.** | Zayıf ihtimal. |
| **The odds are against it / in our favour.** | İhtimaller aleyhimize / lehimize. |
| **Against all odds,** ... | Her şeye rağmen, imkânsız gibi görünse de ... |
| **It's touch and go.** | Belirsiz, ucu ucuna. |
| **It's anyone's guess.** | Kimse bilemez. |
| **I wouldn't bet on it.** | Pek sanmam. |

**Dikkat:**

- *I wouldn't be surprised if* **muhtemel** demek (olumsuz görünse de!)
- *I doubt whether he'll come.* = He probably won't come.
- **I doubt** + olumsuz kullanılmaz: ~~I doubt he won't come~~

examples.en: I wouldn't be surprised if it snowed tonight.
I doubt whether we'll finish on time.
Who will win? It's anyone's guess.

learn.turkishNote: "I wouldn't be surprised if..." ifadesi Türkçedeki "... olsa şaşırmam" ile birebir aynıdır; olumsuz yapıya rağmen "muhtemel" anlamına gelir. "I doubt" ise Türkçedeki "Pek sanmam" ya da "Şüpheliyim" ile örtüşür, yani olumsuz bir tahmindir. "It's anyone's guess" (Kimse bilemez / Allah bilir) çok doğal ve sık kullanılan bir kalıptır.

lessons.title: Geleceği öngörmek
lessons.goal: Farklı kesinlik düzeylerini dengeli kullanarak geleceğe dair gerekçeli ve inandırıcı bir öngörü makalesi yazabilirim.

discover.title: Makale: 2050'de şehirler
discover.body:
What will our cities look like in 2050? Nobody can say for certain, but current trends give us some clues.

Firstly, cities are bound to become larger. According to the United Nations, around two-thirds of the world's population is expected to live in urban areas by 2050. This means that housing is likely to remain one of the biggest challenges.

Transport may well change beyond recognition. Electric and self-driving vehicles are likely to become common, and there is a strong possibility that many city centres will ban private cars altogether. Some cities in Europe have already started.

Climate change, however, is the great unknown. Coastal cities could well face serious flooding, and in all likelihood, many will need to invest heavily in sea defences. Rising temperatures are also likely to make green spaces and trees more important than ever.

Will we all be living in "smart" cities controlled by AI? I doubt it. Technology will undoubtedly play a role, but I would be surprised if it solved problems such as inequality on its own.

In short, the cities of 2050 are likely to be greener, more crowded and more connected. Whether they will also be fairer is anyone's guess.

questions.prompt: What proportion of people are expected to live in cities by 2050?

options: That we'll all live in AI-controlled smart cities
questions.explanation: "Will we all be living in 'smart' cities controlled by AI? I doubt it."

learn.explanation:
**İyi bir öngörü makalesinin özellikleri:**

| Özellik | Örnek |
|---|---|
| **Belirsizliği kabul etmek** | *Nobody can say for certain, but ...* |
| **Kanıta dayanmak** | *According to ..., current trends suggest ...* |
| **Kesinliği derecelendirmek** | En emin olduğundan en az emin olduğuna sıralayın: *bound to → likely to → may well → I doubt* |
| **Bağlam ve neden** | *This means that ... / because ...* |
| **Kendi sesini eklemek** | *I would be surprised if ... / I doubt it.* |
| **Dengeli kapanış** | *In short, ... Whether ... is anyone's guess.* |

**Kaçınılması gerekenler:**

- Her şeyi **kesin** sunmak: ~~Cities will be completely green.~~ → *Cities are likely to be greener.*
- Aynı yapıyı **tekrarlamak**: ~~will probably ... will probably ... will probably~~
- **Kanıtsız** iddialar: Kaynak belirtin ya da "current trends" gibi gerekçe verin.

**Edilgen öngörü yapıları (resmî):**

- *... **is expected to** reach 10 million.*
- *... **is predicted / forecast to** grow by 5%.*
- ***It is estimated that** ...*

(Bu yapıları C1 Ünite 8'de daha ayrıntılı göreceksiniz.)

examples.en: Nobody can say for certain, but current trends give us some clues.
examples.tr: Kimse kesin bir şey söyleyemez ama mevcut eğilimler bize bazı ipuçları veriyor.

examples.en: The population is expected to reach 10 million by 2040.
Whether this will make us happier is anyone's guess.
examples.tr: Bunun bizi daha mutlu edip etmeyeceğini kimse bilemez.

learn.turkishNote: Türkçe makalelerde gelecek tahminleri bazen çok kesin bir dille yapılır ("2050'de şehirler tamamen akıllı olacak"). İngilizce yazı kültüründe ise okuyucu, yazarın ne kadar emin olduğunu bilmek ister; aşırı kesin ifadeler güvenilirliği azaltır. Farklı olasılık yapılarını kullanmak hem dil düzeyinizi gösterir hem de yazınızı daha inandırıcı yapar.

options: Nobody can say for certain, but current trends give us some clues.
Cities are likely to be greener.
The population is expected to double.
Whether they will also be fairer is anyone's guess.

task.prompt: Bir dergi için "Eğitim 2050" ya da "Sağlık 2050" başlıklı bir öngörü makalesi yazın (230–280 kelime). Belirsizliği kabul eden bir girişle başlayın; en az 3 öngörüyü farklı kesinlik düzeyleriyle sunun ve gerekçelendirin. En az 7 farklı olasılık yapısı kullanın (bound to, likely to, may well, It is highly unlikely that, The chances are, I doubt whether, I wouldn't be surprised if, is expected to, in all likelihood). Kendi sesinizi ekleyin ve dengeli bir kapanış yapın.
task.modelAnswer:
Education in 2050

Predicting the future of education is risky. Twenty years ago, few people imagined that millions of students would one day attend classes through their laptops. Nevertheless, current trends suggest a few likely changes.

Firstly, technology is bound to play an even bigger role. Artificial intelligence is likely to become a personal tutor for every student, adapting lessons to their level and giving instant feedback. The chances are that homework, as we know it today, will look very different, since it is becoming harder to know whether students have done it themselves.

Secondly, the idea of finishing education at twenty-two may well disappear. As jobs change faster, most adults are expected to return to learning several times during their careers. In all likelihood, short online courses will become as important as university degrees.

However, some things are unlikely to change. It is highly unlikely that schools will disappear, because children need more than information. They need friends, teachers who care about them and a place to learn how to live with others. I doubt whether any machine will be able to replace that.

There are also risks. If access to technology remains unequal, the gap between rich and poor students could well grow. I wouldn't be surprised if this became one of the most important political debates of the next decade.

In short, the classroom of 2050 is likely to be more flexible, more personal and more digital. Whether it will also be more human depends on the choices we make today.

questions.prompt: "Çalışma hayatı 2040" konulu bir blog yazısı yazın (220–260 kelime). Belirsizliği kabul eden bir girişle başlayın; uzaktan çalışma, yapay zekâ ve çalışma saatleri konularında öngörülerde bulunun. En az 7 farklı olasılık yapısı kullanın ve her öngörüyü gerekçelendirin. Bir yerde geçmişe dair bir olasılık yapısı (may well have, is likely to have) kullanın ve dengeli bir kapanış yapın.
questions.modelAnswer:
Work in 2040: what's coming?

If anyone had told us in 2015 that millions of people would soon be working from their kitchens, few of us would have believed them. The pandemic may well have changed the world of work more in two years than the previous twenty. So what comes next? Nobody can say for certain, but here are my predictions.

Firstly, remote and hybrid work are bound to remain common. Most companies have already invested in the technology, and many employees are unlikely to accept a return to five days in the office. The chances are that offices will become places for meetings and teamwork, rather than for everyday tasks.

Secondly, artificial intelligence is likely to change almost every job. Routine tasks such as writing reports or analysing data may well be done mostly by machines. However, it is highly unlikely that AI will replace people completely. Instead, workers will in all likelihood need to learn how to work alongside it.

Finally, I wouldn't be surprised if the four-day week became normal in many countries. Several trials have shown that productivity doesn't fall when people work fewer hours. That said, I doubt whether every industry will be able to adopt it.

Of course, these changes won't benefit everyone equally. Workers without digital skills could well be left behind.

In short, the job market of 2040 is likely to be more flexible and more digital. Whether it will also be fairer is, for now, anyone's guess.
